chapter_title: Univariate Data: Box Plots, Quartiles, and Standard Deviation (10 & 10A)

worksheets.title: Box Plots, Outlier Fences, and Comparing Distributions

fluency_questions.prompt: For the ordered dataset of $11$ test scores: $42, 48, 51, 55, 58, 62, 66, 70, 74, 79, 85$, find:

parts.label: b
parts.question: The lower quartile ($Q_1$) and upper quartile ($Q_3$)

fluency_questions.prompt: A distribution has five-number summary $\text{Min} = 8$, $Q_1 = 24$, $\text{Median} = 30$, $Q_3 = 36$, $\text{Max} = 58$. Find:

parts.label: d
parts.question: Which extreme value ($8$ or $58$) is a formal outlier

fluency_questions.prompt: For a box-and-whisker plot with $\text{Min} = 10$, $Q_1 = 20$, $Q_2 = 25$, $Q_3 = 40$, $\text{Max} = 60$ (no outliers), state:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The percentage of data values that lie between $Q_1 = 20$ and $Q_3 = 40$

parts.label: b
parts.question: The percentage of data values that lie above $Q_1 = 20$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Whether the distribution is symmetric, positively skewed, or negatively skewed
parts.answer: Positively skewed (right whisker and upper half of box are longer)

parts.label: d
parts.question: Which measure of centre and spread is most appropriate for this skewed distribution

fluency_questions.prompt: [10A] For the sample of $n = 5$ values: $4, 7, 10, 13, 16$, calculate:

parts.label: d
parts.question: The sample standard deviation $s = \sqrt{s^2}$ in exact surd form and to $2$ d.p.

application_questions.question: Daily maximum temperatures ($^\circ\text{C}$) recorded over $9$ days in Mildura are: $21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, 41$. Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$, the $\text{IQR}$, and the upper fence $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ to determine whether the $41^\circ\text{C}$ heatwave day is a statistical outlier.
application_questions.answer: $Q_1 = 23.5$, $Q_3 = 29.5$, $\text{IQR} = 6.0$; upper fence $= 29.5 + 1.5(6.0) = 38.5^\circ\text{C}$. Since $41 > 38.5$, $41^\circ\text{C}$ is an outlier.

application_questions.question: Parallel box plots compare commuting times (minutes) for $120$ train passengers and $120$ bus passengers in Sydney. For train passengers: $\text{Min} = 15, Q_1 = 25, \text{Med} = 32, Q_3 = 40, \text{Max} = 55$. How many train passengers had a commute of $40\text{ minutes}$ or less, and what is the $\text{IQR}$?

House prices in a coastal Victorian town have a strongly positively skewed distribution due to a few luxury clifftop mansions. Which is larger—the mean or the median—and why do real-estate reports quote the median house price instead of the mean?
application_questions.answer: The mean is larger because high-value outliers pull the mean upwards; the median is quoted because it is resistant to extreme outliers.

application_questions.question: [10A] Two coffee machines in a Melbourne café dispense espresso shots with the same mean volume of $30\text{ mL}$, but Machine A has standard deviation $s_A = 0.8\text{ mL}$ and Machine B has $s_B = 2.5\text{ mL}$. Which machine is more consistent, and what would happen to $s_A$ if every shot from Machine A were increased by exactly $5\text{ mL}$?
application_questions.answer: Machine A is more consistent ($s_A < s_B$). Adding $5\text{ mL}$ to every value shifts the mean to $35\text{ mL}$ but leaves the standard deviation $s_A = 0.8\text{ mL}$ unchanged.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why the interquartile range ($\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$) is considered a **resistant** measure of spread, whereas the range ($\text{Max} - \text{Min}$) and standard deviation $s$ are not resistant to outliers.
reasoning_questions.answer: The $\text{IQR}$ depends only on the middle $50\%$ of the ordered data ($Q_1$ and $Q_3$), so changing the maximum or minimum to an extreme outlier does not affect the $\text{IQR}$, whereas the range and $\sum(x_i - \bar{x})^2$ increase substantially.

reasoning_questions.question: [10A] Prove that for any sample dataset, the sample standard deviation $s = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}$ equals $0$ if and only if all data values in the sample are identical.
reasoning_questions.answer: Since every squared term $(x_i - \bar{x})^2 \ge 0$, their sum is $0$ if and only if $x_i - \bar{x} = 0$ for every $i$, which means $x_1 = x_2 = \dots = x_n = \bar{x}$.
